headline: Android's hidden security upgrade disabled by default on all phones
summary: Critical security features like Theft Detection Lock and enhanced Chrome browsing are turned off by default, leaving millions of Android users vulnerable.
details: Android 16 launched with an 'Advanced Protection' security upgrade, but it's disabled by default on all devices. This suite of features includes protections like Theft Detection Lock, which locks your phone if motion indicates theft, and enhanced Chrome browsing that warns you about non-HTTPS sites.

The Advanced Protection toggle also blocks unknown app sources and disables Watch Unlock. While these features might cause minor inconveniences, they offer a significant boost to your phone's overall security and data protection.

Beyond security, tweaking background processes can improve performance. Disabling unnecessary background data can free up to 2GB of RAM, boost battery life, and enhance overall device performance, though it may slightly delay notifications and app launches.

For a smoother experience, adjusting animation scales in Developer Options is key. Settings like Window animation scale, Transition animation scale, and Animator duration scale can drastically speed up app opening times without making transitions feel abrupt.

Enabling Developer Options requires tapping the 'Build Number' seven times in your phone's 'About Phone' settings. Once enabled, you can access these performance-enhancing tweaks and security settings.

While ideally these crucial settings would be enabled during the initial phone setup, they can all be activated in under a minute once you know where to look, significantly improving your Android experience.

headline: Scimplify raises $25M to challenge China's grip on critical materials with AI
summary: The Indian startup is using AI to speed up the production of specialty chemicals and critical materials, aiming to reduce reliance on Chinese suppliers.
details: Scimplify, an Indian startup focused on AI-driven production of specialty chemicals and critical materials, has secured $25 million in an all-equity strategic funding round. The investment, led by Hitachi Ventures with participation from customers like Henkel and Teknor Apex, values the company at $250 million.

The startup aims to challenge China's dominance in critical materials supply chains, targeting sectors such as semiconductors, defense, and energy. Scimplify's proprietary AI platform, Scinode, helps identify suitable production routes and manufacturing facilities, significantly shortening the time from customer requirement to material delivery.

Traditionally, developing and delivering new materials can take 12 to 18 months. Scimplify has demonstrated the ability to deliver finished materials in as little as two months by leveraging its AI platform and a network of over 500 partner factories, primarily in India.

The company's annualized revenue run rate has surged to approximately $200 million, tripling from the previous year. Scimplify plans to expand its production network to the U.S. and Japan within the next year, with the U.S. market alone contributing significantly to its revenue growth.

Scimplify's focus areas include tungsten derivatives and rare earth materials, both categories heavily influenced by Chinese supply chains. By offering alternative sources, the startup is positioning itself as a key player in diversifying global material sourcing.

The company serves over 1,000 customers globally and has delivered products to more than 40 countries. Scimplify has also achieved EBITDA positivity for the past two months and anticipates becoming profitable after tax this month.
